I'm away at the moment - will investigate further next week. 

However I have a nasty feeling that uploads don't work with ACD via fuse because they need to know the file size in advance.

Yes I've confirmed this - you can't upload files to ACD with `rclone mount`. :-(  This is rather complicated to fix unfortunately - it might just be easier it I add a flag so rclone mount uses a temporary file for the upload.

body: I am experiencing a quite similar issue with fuse mount, but the behaviour seems to depend on the operating system. In Ubuntu 14.04, fuse mount works fine (I can create or copy files without apparent restrictions), while fuse mount in Raspbian Jessie behaves as if it were a read-only filesystem. In both systems rclone copy/sync are working properly.

Same issue here.

```
$ rclone -V
rclone v1.33-105-gd1080d5β
```

```
$ cp twrp_z00a_v24_repack.img ~/acd/
cp: impossibile creare il file regolare '/home/niccolo/acd/twrp_z00a_v24_repack.img': Errore di input/output
```

Hope you will fix it soon, meanwhile i'm going to use acd_cli to upload.

Hm, I guess I _must_ be missing something here. AmazonDrive does not require the size to be known in advance, apart from the "files over 12 GB might not work" check. Using this rather simple patch, I can do the following:

```
$ cp /opt/rclone ~/acd/                                            
$ md5sum /opt/rclone                                               
505cfe704e2f7faf5b84104e86f68323  /opt/rclone
$ md5sum ~/acd/rclone                                               
505cfe704e2f7faf5b84104e86f68323  /home/stefan/acd/rclone
$ rm ~/acd/rclone                                                  
$ cat /opt/rclone > ~/acd/rclone                                   
$ md5sum ~/acd/rclone                                              
505cfe704e2f7faf5b84104e86f68323  /home/stefan/acd/rclone
```

Overwriting doesn't work yet, but I haven't checked where this issue stems from. I first wanted to know what other problems you had in mind that would make write support complicated before fixing any of the probably simple bugs?

The patch is simply explained: instead of relying on `src` to give us a size, it simply checks if at least one byte can be read. The `PutSized` is only needed to create 0-byte files anyway.

```
diff --git a/amazonclouddrive/amazonclouddrive.go b/amazonclouddrive/amazonclouddrive.go
index 2a4d1a9..61ffde7 100644
--- a/amazonclouddrive/amazonclouddrive.go
+++ b/amazonclouddrive/amazonclouddrive.go
@@ -13,6 +13,7 @@ we ignore assets completely!
 */

 import (
+ "bytes"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "io"
@@ -590,10 +591,14 @@ func (f *Fs) Put(in io.Reader, src fs.ObjectInfo) (fs.Object, error) {
        err = f.pacer.CallNoRetry(func() (bool, error) {
                start := time.Now()
                f.startUpload()
-           if src.Size() != 0 {
-                   info, resp, err = folder.Put(in, leaf)
-           } else {
+
+         buf := make([]byte, 1)
+         n, readErr := in.Read(buf)
+         if n == 0 && readErr == io.EOF {
                        info, resp, err = folder.PutSized(in, size, leaf)
+         } else {
+                 in = io.MultiReader(bytes.NewReader(buf), in)
+                 info, resp, err = folder.Put(in, leaf)
                }
                f.stopUpload()
                var ok bool
```

issue.body:
Hi,

I was trying to write to a acd mount point and kept getting the following type of errors `WriteFileHandle.Flush error: Post https://content-eu.drive.amazonaws.com/cdproxy/nodes?suppress=deduplication: http: ContentLength=486 with Body length 57546611`. I found https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/813 which explained the problem as 

> This is because Amazon need to know the size of the file in advance for the upload, but we don't know it until the end.

Can you explain this problem in some more detail please because i also read https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/669 which seems to suggest that the file size isn't required in advance. 

Looking through the acd API documentation it does mention [here](https://developer.amazon.com/public/apis/experience/cloud-drive/content/restful-api-getting-started) that the size **is** required.

> Content-Length	Specifies the length of the message in the body; without the headers. This is a required parameter when the body of the request in not empty.

Fingers crossed that write support is possible on `mount` to allow use of common tools/scripts to shift data into acd like `cp` or `rsync` etc..

Out of curiosity... in the fuse code when you receive the request would it not be possible to use the target file name that your about to create/write via rclone and scan the associated local source path for the matching file and stat the file size to fulfill acd requirement to specify size on upload ? Or is that a bit willy wonka thinking ?

Great project, thanks for all your hard work.
